resource.title: Resource
resource.description: UKG Pro WFM resource to extract (one resource per configuration row).

window_type.title: Date Selection
window_type.description: Choose the fetch window by explicit dates or by a rolling symbolic period

options.tooltip: Date range: set an explicit Start Date / End Date window. Symbolic period: use a UKG rolling period (e.g. Current Pay Period) that resolves the range for you. Symbolic periods are not supported for scheduling resources — use a date range there.

load_type.title: Load Type
load_type.description: How rows are written to the table: full load replaces it each run; incremental load upserts by primary key

options.tooltip: This controls the Storage write mode only, not how much data is fetched — the fetch window is set by Start/End Date. Incremental load upserts by the Primary Key; a resource with no primary key always runs as a full replace.

since.title: Start Date
since.description: Lower bound of the fetch window

options.tooltip: ISO 8601 (e.g. `2026-01-01T00:00:00+00:00`) or a relative phrase (e.g. `30 days ago`, `yesterday`). Applied on every run as the lower bound of the fetch window — Load Type only changes how rows are written to Storage, not which data is fetched.

until.title: End Date
until.description: Upper bound of the fetch window

options.tooltip: Optional. ISO 8601 (e.g. `2026-02-01T00:00:00+00:00`) or a relative phrase (e.g. `yesterday`, `now`). Leave empty to fetch up to the current run time; set it to bound a backfill to a fixed window.

window_days.title: Window Chunk Size (days)
window_days.description: Split the Start/End window into chunks of at most this many days, fetched one at a time.

options.tooltip: Optional. For a large date range on a per-event resource (schedules, shifts, timecards, leave, attendance, attestations), lower this to pull the data in smaller pieces so the job stays under the memory limit — each chunk is fetched and written separately. Leave empty for the default (365 days). NOT for rollup resources (Timecard Metrics, Accruals), which return one total per employee — control their memory with a smaller employee batch instead. Punch-level resources always use their own per-request cap.

batch_size.title: Employee Batch Size
batch_size.description: Employees fetched per API request. Lower it if a run hits the 256 MB memory limit.

options.tooltip: Optional. Number of employees sent per multi_read request. The whole batch response is parsed into memory at once, so if a run fails with 'out of memory (exceeded 256M)' — most likely on Timecard Metrics or Accruals over a wide date range — lower this (e.g. to 25). It is the primary memory lever for rollup resources (Timecard Metrics, Accruals), which cannot be split by date the way per-event resources can with Window Chunk Size. Trade-off: fewer employees per request means more requests, so the run is slower. Leave empty for the per-resource default (Timecard Metrics and Punches 100; Accruals and most per-event resources 500; activity net-changes 50). Ignored by resources that are not employee-scoped (e.g. Persons, Business Structure).

The SQL-like query UKG WFM runs for the async payroll export (POST /commons/payroll/export/async). It is tenant-specific — use the export query your WFM tenant defines. Required for the Payroll Export resource.

hyperfind_ref.title: Hyperfind Query
hyperfind_ref.description: Employee set this resource is pulled for

options.tooltip: The Hyperfind query that resolves which employees this resource extracts. Click Load Hyperfinds and pick from the tenant's saved queries (public, personal, and system). Leave unset to fall back to 'All Home', which large tenants reject above their size threshold — pick a narrower query instead.

hyperfind_threshold.title: Hyperfind Threshold
hyperfind_threshold.description: Maximum number of employees the Hyperfind Query above may resolve before the request is rejected.

options.tooltip: UKG rejects a Hyperfind that resolves more employees than this cap with error WCO-112003. UKG's per-request default is low, so a broad Hyperfind ('All Home'/'All People') fails unless it is raised. If left empty, the component applies 50000 — raise it only if your tenant roster is larger, or lower it to cap the roster deliberately.

metric_group.title: Timecard Metric Group
metric_group.description: The one metric group (select token) to pull for Timekeeping — Timecard Metrics. Its line items are exploded into one row per item (with applyDate and a uniqueId primary key). Exactly one group is required for this resource.

options.tooltip: Pick the one metric group you need. Its response section is exploded into per-line-item rows (with applyDate and a uniqueId primary key). Leaving it unset is not allowed for this resource — an empty selection would return every section, which cannot be exploded into one table.

symbolic_period.title: Symbolic Period
symbolic_period.description: Rolling period window (e.g. Current Pay Period) used instead of an explicit start/end date window

options.tooltip: The UKG-named rolling period range (e.g. `Current Pay Period`, `Previous Pay Period`, `Yesterday`, `Today`). Click Load Symbolic Periods and pick from the tenant's periods; the value stored is the numeric id — WFM rejects a period name, only the id works. Not supported for scheduling resources (they require a Date range). See the UKG Pro WFM API reference: https://developer.ukg.com/wfm/reference

primary_key.title: Primary Key
primary_key.description: Column(s) that identify a row for upsert. The API returns no field list, so columns are read from Storage after the first run — run once then Re-load, or type them.

options.tooltip: On incremental load the component upserts on these columns. The WFM API doesn't expose a field list, so the picker reads columns from this resource's output table in Storage — which exists only after the first run. Run once, then click Re-load Columns from Storage; or type the column name(s) directly (before the first run, on a dev branch, or with a custom output bucket). Supplying a key also enables upsert for a resource with no registry default. Empty = the resource's registry default.

max_wait_seconds.title: Payroll Max Wait (seconds)
max_wait_seconds.description: Maximum time to poll a Payroll async export before failing (avoids hanging).

options.tooltip: If left empty, the component waits up to 1800 seconds (30 minutes) before failing the poll.

poll_interval_seconds.title: Payroll Poll Interval (seconds)
poll_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between Payroll async export status polls.

options.tooltip: If left empty, the component polls every 15 seconds.
